before: Undo could export empty numbering definition shells and omit the retained numbering content type from saved bytes.
after: Undo retains allocation data for delayed references, marks unused definitions unavailable, and restores needed definitions with existing shared updates. Saved bytes retain the numbering content type.
reason: The wire schema and identities do not change. Allocation attributes and children remain ordinary existing data. Existing undone marks still mean unavailable; restoring a live dependency removes that mark using the existing restore origin. Released readers understand these records and mark removals. The content-type repair reconciles saved bytes with the existing authoritative metadata index without shared writes.
